items.title: RBA expected to pause rate hikes as economist fears 'downturn'
items.description: The unemployment rate rose by 0.2 percentage points to 4.5 per cent in April, up from 4.3 per cent in March, according to the Bureau of Statistics.

items.title: Worst diphtheria outbreak on record spurs $7m federal vaccine response
items.description: The federal government has stepped in to address the largest diphtheria outbreak since records began, unveiling a multi-million dollar package for more vaccines and workers to deliver them.

items.title: Australia backs landmark UN climate change ruling as others try to block it
items.description: Australia joins 140 other countries in passing a major United Nations resolution backing a landmark legal ruling on climate change, despite efforts by the United States, Russia and Saudi Arabia to sink it.

items.title: NDIS whistleblower protections 'among worst in the country', inquiry told
items.description: A raft of alarming evidence has been aired at a parliamentary hearing into the integrity of the NDIS, with calls for the government to strengthen whistleblower protections.

items.title: Warning about 'fraudulent' Apple gift cards bought at Coles supermarket
items.description: Coles is looking into a Melbourne mother's complaint about buying faulty Apple gift cards worth $2,000.

items.title: Musk's X ordered to pay $750,000 for not complying with Australian child protection request
items.description: Elon ​Musk's social media company X Corp has ​admitted ‌to not complying with an order from Australia's eSafety commissioner to ⁠provide information about the measures it has in place ​to stop ‌child exploitation on the X platform.

items.title: How Australia's EV uptake compares with the rest of the world
items.description: High petrol prices are driving EV sales around the world, with the leading international authority predicting 30 per cent of all new cars sold this year will be electric.

items.title: Israel's government supported Ben-Gvir's callousness, until it didn't
items.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has condemned a video of his national security minister taunting activists, including Australians, who have been detained. But it's the prime minister who allowed this behaviour to percolate.

items.title: Queensland Olympics minister referred to AFP over voting registration
items.description: The Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) confirmed on Thursday it had made the referral.

items.title: Woman dies after being hit by police car in Cairns
items.description: A 71-year-old woman has died after being hit by a police car in Cairns this morning.

items.title: Arrow's MND diagnosis shines spotlight on debilitating condition that has no cure
items.description: As another rugby league player is diagnosed with motor neurone disease, we asked experts why so little is known about what causes it.

items.title: Results are out for the world's most powerful company, but investors aren't impressed
items.description: The world's most valuable company, tech giant Nvidia, has reported a record revenue but investors are not impressed with second-quarter sales forecasts.

items.title: As Colbert wraps up The Late Show, late-night TV could be on shaky ground
items.description: Like other checks and balances on presidential power, late-night talk shows — once ratings juggernauts, woven into the fabric of American culture — are being stress-tested. Here's how they became a staging ground for the battle over free speech.

items.title: Kylie Minogue doco reveals second cancer diagnosis, IVF struggles, and more
items.description: "Our Kylie" gets candid in the three-part Netflix docuseries, grieving over IVF struggles, Michael Hutchence, and revealing she was diagnosed with cancer a second time in 2021.

items.title: What are the signs of broken heart syndrome?
items.description: Experts say broken heart syndrome accounts for about two per cent of patients presenting with symptoms similar to a heart attack.

items.title: Think you know music and film? Let's see how well you score in this quiz
items.description: From Mozart to Max Richter, can you pick the classical music in these iconic films?

items.title: Arafura Rare Earths mine gets green light to challenge China's dominance
items.description: Arafura Rare Earths has announced its flagship project north of Alice Springs will go ahead, decades after it was first flagged as a prospect.

items.title: Government to slash 1,700 jobs as Abetz looks to rein in Tasmanian spending
items.description: The Tasmanian government will slash 1,700 jobs through natural attrition and negotiated voluntary redundancies, as Treasurer Eric Abetz unveils his second state budget.

items.title: Fears CSIRO job cuts will damage Australia's climate change adaptability
items.description: Some CSIRO staff are concerned the science agency's plan to cut 92 jobs, predominantly from its environment and climate science division, will negatively affect Australia's ability to assess and adapt to climate change.

items.title: 'Shocking': Wife of Bondi victim reacts as man accused of stealing camera
items.description: A photographer who allegedly stole a camera from a Bondi terror attack victim before pawning it days later has been charged.

items.title: Former NSW Young Australian of the Year dies aged 32
items.description: Nikhil Autar, who was diagnosed with leukaemia when he was 17 years old, was named NSW Young Australian of the Year in 2024.

items.title: Female AFL creators say vile comments 'just one example of what we deal with'
items.description: A video circulated across social media of a group of men laughing about how one of them would "beat the f***" out of a group of female content creators.

items.title: Australian parents in 'survival mode all the time' break taboos on raising kids
items.description: As the birth rate hits a record low it's been revealed that almost 60 per cent of Australian parents are experiencing psychological distress, according to the largest-ever national parenting survey.

items.title: Snowtown killer James Vlassakis's image has been revealed. Here's why
items.description: The youngest of the Snowtown killers was the subject of a long-running suppression order that kept his face — or any description of his appearance — hidden for 25 years. Here's why that's been lifted.

items.title: Peak body slams ministers' failure to attend Aboriginal housing talks
items.description: The Northern Territory's peak body for Aboriginal housing says it's "disgraceful" ministers from both levels of government have failed to attend a conference on the housing crisis.
